Patient demographics:

  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Carpenter

  pcl5: 42

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Rumination: Self-Blame: repeatedly blame myself for what happened, Drug Use: take drugs, Avoid Thinking: Thinking about the event
  Threat: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room, Threat in Delays: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Vignette:
Thanh was a 31-year-old South Eastern Asian man who sought help for the persistent anxiety and intrusive thoughts he had experienced since a traumatic encounter with law enforcement. Married and working as a carpenter in his local community, Thanh's life had been upended by an incident that left him feeling perpetually unsafe. The trauma began on what should have been another ordinary day at work. On that fateful afternoon, while working alone in an abandoned warehouse to complete a project for a client, Thanh was confronted by two police officers who mistook him for someone else. Despite his repeated explanations and attempts to show identification, the officers grew increasingly agitated. One officer drew his weapon and pointed it at Thanh, forcing him against the wall with their gun pressed to his head. The fear and helplessness he felt during those moments were indelibly imprinted in his mind. In the aftermath of this encounter, Thanh began to ruminate on what had happened, repeatedly blaming himself for not doing more to de-escalate the situation or prevent it from occurring at all. He would often find himself replaying the scene over and over again, questioning if he could have acted differently to avoid such a terrifying outcome. The incident also triggered Thanh’s reliance on drug use as a maladaptive coping mechanism. On many nights, he found solace in substances that dulled his senses and temporarily eased his anxiety. However, this only provided fleeting relief, and the underlying fears persisted. Thanh's desire to avoid thinking about the traumatic event led him to actively steer clear of any scenarios that might trigger memories or reminders. He stopped working alone and avoided isolated areas, which limited his ability to take on certain projects that required solitude for concentration and focus. One of Thanh’s primary fears was feeling unsafe unless his back was against a wall where he could see the entire room. This hyper-vigilance extended into his daily life, making him uneasy in environments where he couldn’t maintain complete visual control over his surroundings. At work, this meant he preferred to be in more open areas with fewer blind spots, which sometimes created tension with other workers who felt he was avoiding certain tasks or spaces. Another manifestation of Thanh’s heightened sense of threat was his tendency to assume the worst when something took longer than expected. For instance, if a delivery for work was delayed by even a few minutes, he would immediately worry that something bad had happened. This anxiety often led him to call his wife multiple times during the day to check in and ensure her safety. Thanh found it incredibly challenging to relax even in safe environments. He was unable to fully unwind or enjoy time with friends and family because of persistent feelings of unease and impending danger. His marriage began to suffer as well, as he became increasingly isolated and irritable, which put a strain on his relationship with his wife. It wasn't until one particularly harrowing incident at work, where Thanh’s panic attack left him unable to complete a job in time for the client's deadline, that he realized he needed help. The fear of losing his job and straining his marriage further was too much to bear. He had come to believe that he would never be able to shake off the haunting memories and the sense of perpetual danger. Thanh sought therapy with hope that he could regain a semblance of control over his life. What frightened him most was the prospect of living in constant fear, unable to trust even his own home or workplace as safe havens. He was certain that without intervention, this unrelenting anxiety would continue to erode his quality of life and relationships. Thanh was hoping for a way to find peace and regain confidence in himself and his surroundings, free from the shadow of past trauma.
